$∴ 5 ( 1 + x ) = 9x$

$∴ 5 + 5x = 9x$

$∴ 5 = 4x$

$∴ x = \dfrac{5}{4}Ω$

$∴ x = 1 . 25Ω$

questions.q: In a Wheatstone's network, $P = 2Ω$, $Q = 2Ω$, $R = 2Ω$ and $S = 3Ω$. Find the resistance (in $Ω$) with which $S$ is to be shunted, in order that the bridge gets balanced.
questions.solution:
Let a resistance $rΩ$ be shunted with resistance $S$, so that the bridge is balanced.

Let $S '$ be the resultant resistance of $S$ and $r$, then

In balanced position



$\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{R}{{S}^{′}}$

$\dfrac{2}{2} = \dfrac{2}{{S}^{′}}$

$∴ {S}^{′} = 2Ω$

Now,

$\dfrac{1}{{S}^{′}} = \dfrac{1}{S} + \dfrac{1}{r}$

$\dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{{S}^{′}} - \dfrac{1}{S} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{6}$

$\dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$r = 6Ω$

questions.q: The figure shows an $RC$ circuit with a parallel plate capacitor. Before switching on the circuit, plate $A$ of the capacitor has a charge $- {Q}_{0}$ while plate $B$ has no net charge. If at $t = 0$, the switch is closed then after how much time (in seconds) will the net charge on plate A becomes zero?[Given: $C = 1\mu F$, ${Q}_{0} = 1mC$, $ε = 1000V$ and $R = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{6}}{ln3}Ω$]
questions.solution:
Let at any time $t$ the charge that flows from the plate $B$ to plate $A$ is $q$ and the instantaneous current is $I$.

$\left(\dfrac{2q - {Q}_{0}}{2C}\right) + IR - ε = 0$

$⇒ R\dfrac{dq}{dt} = \dfrac{- 2q + 2εC + {Q}_{0}}{2C}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dq}{2εC + {Q}_{0} - 2q} = \dfrac{dt}{2RC}$

Now for the charge on plate $A$ to be zero $q = {Q}_{0}$.

${∫}_{0}^{{Q}_{0}}\dfrac{dq}{2εC + {Q}_{0} - 2q} = {∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{2RC}$

$⇒ t = RCln\left[\dfrac{2εC + {Q}_{0}}{2εC - {Q}_{0}}\right] = 2s$

questions.q: An electric current passes through a circuit containing two wires of the same material connected in parallel. If the lengths of the wires are in the ratio $\dfrac{4}{3}$ and radius of the wires are in the ratio $\dfrac{2}{3}$, then the ratio of the current passing through the wires is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are smallest integers. What is $m + n$?
questions.solution:
Given that,

$\dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}} = \dfrac{4}{3}and\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Here, ${l}_{1}$and ${l}_{2}$are the length of the wires while ${r}_{1}$and ${r}_{2}$ are the radii of the wires.

Now, we know that

$V = IR ⟹ IR = constant$

$⟹ {I}_{1}{R}_{1} = {I}_{2}{R}_{2}$

$or\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}} \ldots . \left(i\right)$

But we know that the resistance of the wire is

$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$

Hence, from Eq (i)

$\dfrac{{I ⁡}_{1}}{{I ⁡}_{2}} = \dfrac{ρ {l ⁡}_{2} / {A ⁡}_{2}}{ρ {l ⁡}_{1} / {A ⁡}_{1}}$

Here,

${R}_{1} = \dfrac{ρ{l}_{1}}{{A}_{1}}, {R}_{2} = \dfrac{ρ{l}_{2}}{{A}_{2}}and{ρ}_{1} = {ρ}_{2} = ρ$

Because both wires are of same material.

$∴ \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{2}{A}_{1}}{{l}_{1}{A}_{2}}$

$⟹ \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{2}\pi{r}_{1}^{2}}{{l}_{1}\pi{r}_{2}^{2}}$

$⟹ \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{2}{r}_{1}^{2}}{{l}_{1}{r}_{2}^{2}}$

Here, $\dfrac{{l}_{2}}{{l}_{1}} = \dfrac{3}{4}and\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⟹ \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times {\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{2}$

Or $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{m}{n} ⇒ m + n = 4$

questions.q: Two cylindrical conductors with equal cross-sections and different resistivities ${ρ}_{1}$ and ${ρ}_{2}$ are put end to end. Find the charge at the boundary of the conductors if a current $I$ flows from conductor $1$ to conductor $2$._{}
questions.solution:
According to ohm's law,$\overset{→}{E}=\text{ρ}\overset{→}{J}$

The problem is solved by the following steps:

Step I: Determine the electric field in both conductors.

The current density in the first conductor is

${J}_{1}=\dfrac{I}{\text{\pi}R^{2}}$(Along the length of the conductor)



Similarly,${J}_{2}=\dfrac{I}{\text{\pi}R^{2}}$ (along the length of the conductor)

The electric field inside the first conductor is
${E}_{2}=\dfrac{{ρ}_{2}\text{I}}{\text{\pi}R^{2}}$(along the length of the conductor)

Step II: Consider small cylindrical region near the boundary and apply Gauss's law:

We consider a small cylindrical region at the boundary



The area of the cylindrical region is

$S=\piR^{2}$ &
The net flux through this region is

$\text{ϕ}={ϕ}_{1} + {ϕ}_{2}={\overset{→}{E}}_{1}. \overset{→}{S} + {\overset{→}{E}}_{2} \overset{→}{S}$

$={E}_{1}Scos180 ° + {E}_{2}Scos0 °=- {E}_{1}S + {E}_{2}S=( {E}_{2} - {E}_{1} ) S$

According to Gauss's Law,

$\text{ϕ}=\dfrac{\text{q}}{{ε}_{0}}$

$\text{or} \left({E}_{2} - {E}_{1}\right)=\dfrac{\text{q}}{\text{S} {ε}_{0}}=\dfrac{\text{\sigma}}{{ε}_{0}}$

∴ The surface charge density at the boundary is

$\sigma=( {E}_{2} - {E}_{1} ) {ε}_{0}$

Putting the value of E_{1}_{}and E_{2}, we get

$∴ \sigma=( {ρ}_{2}j - {ρ}_{1}j ) or\sigma=( {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} ) j$

$∴ \text{\sigma}={ε}_{0} \left({ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1}\right) \dfrac{\text{I}}{\text{\pi} R^{2}}$

or $\sigma\piR^{2}={ε}_{0} ( {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} ) I$

or $q={ε}_{0} ( {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} ) I$

Charge at the boundary $q={ε}_{0} ( {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} ) I$

The power of the battery, when charged is given by

The electrical energy dissipated is given by

$= 1050Wh$

$η = \dfrac{{E}_{2}}{{E}_{1}} \times 100$

$= 0.875 \times 100 = 87.5%$
